source_text:
Σομορὼν μὲν οὖν ἐκλήθη τὸ ὄρος, καὶ τὰ ὁμοροῦντα, ἀπὸ Σεμὴρ ἑνὸς υἱοῦ

τῶν Χαναναίων, πρὶν ἢ ἐπιβῆναι τὸν Ἀβραὰμ τῇ γῇ. Ἐλθόντων δὲ τῶν φυλακῶν,
ἐκλήθησαν Σαμαρεῖται, τουτέστι, φύλα89.597 κες. Φύλακες δὲ ἦσαν οὐ μόνον τῆς
γῆς, ἀλλὰ καὶ τοῦ νόμου· ἐφύλαττον γὰρ τὴν Πεντάτευχον μόνην, ἣν ἔλαβον διὰ
Ἔσδρα τοῦ βασιλέως, ἵνα ἐκ τούτου διακρίνηται τὸ σπέρμα τοῦ Ἀβραάμ. Ἀλλ' οὐ
τελείως τὸν νόμον ἐφύλαττον· διό φησιν ἡ Γραφή· "Ἔμειναν ποιοῦντες τὸν νόμον
τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ προσκυνοῦντες τὰ εἴδωλα."
Τοῦ δὲ νόμου κελεύοντος εἴδωλα μὴ προσκυνεῖσθαι, πῶς ἔτι πληρωθήσεται;
Ἔχει δὲ ἡ ὑπόθεσις τὸν τρόπον τοῦτον· Γνόντες γὰρ οἱ μιερεῖς τῶν τεσσάρων ἐθνῶν,
ὅτι ἐνεδήμησεν Ἔσδρας, βδελυττόμενος τὰ εἴδωλα κατὰ τὸν νόμον Θεοῦ,
σπεύσαντες ἔκρυψαν τὰ εἴδωλα ἐν τῷ Γαρίζῃ ὄρει ἐν μυχῷ τινι, καὶ ἀπέστρεψαν τὴν
καρδίαν τῶν Σαμαρειτῶν πρὸς τὸ ὄρος εὔχεσθαι. Ὅθεν, ὅπου δ' ἂν ὦσι, πρὸς τὸ ὄρος
εὔχονται οἱ ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς πρὸς δυσμὰς ἀποστρεφόμενοι, καὶ ἀπὸ δυσμῶν πρὸς
ἀνατολὰς, καὶ ἀπὸ βοῤῥᾶς πρὸς τὴν μεσημβρίαν, πρὸς τὸ ἀρκτῷον τῷ ὄρει
προσέχοντες εὔχονται, ἵνα πληρωθῇ ἡ Γραφὴ, ἡ λέγουσα· "Ἔμειναν ποιοῦντες τὸν
νόμον τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ προσκυνοῦντες αὐτῶν τὰ εἴδωλα." Εἰ γὰρ καὶ αὐτοὶ ἀγνοοῦσι
κειμένων τῶν εἰδώλων ἐκεῖσε, ἀλλ' οὐ δυνατόν ἐστι τὴν θείαν Γραφὴν ψεύσασθαι.
thought_title: Why Samaritans keep the law yet worship idols
orientation: Epiphanius finishes by explaining where the Samaritans came from and how their prayer toward Mount Garizim fulfills Scripture.
pass_a_gloss: Now Mount Somoron was called, and the neighboring regions, from Semer one son of the Canaanites, before Abraham set foot upon the land. And when the guards came, they were called Samaritans, that is, guards. And they were guards not only of the land, but also of the law; for they kept the Pentateuch alone, which they received through Ezra the king, in order that from this the seed of Abraham might be distinguished. But they did not keep the law completely; therefore Scripture says: "They remained doing the law of God, and worshipping the idols." But while the law commands idols not to be worshipped, how will it still be fulfilled? And the underlying account has this manner: for when the impure ones of the four nations knew that Ezra settled here, abhorring the idols according to the law of God, having hastened they hid the idols in Mount Garizim in some recess, and they turned back the heart of the Samaritans toward the mountain to pray. Whence, wherever they are, toward the mountain they pray, those from the east turning away toward the west, and from the west toward the east, and from the north toward the south, holding attention toward the northern part at the mountain they pray, in order that the Scripture might be fulfilled, which says: "They remained doing the law of God, and worshipping their idols." For even if they themselves do not know the idols lying there, yet it is not possible for the divine Scripture to lie.

choices.english: the impure ones of the four nations
choices.why: μιερεῖς spells a form of miaros, impure/abominable, not hiereis, priests; literal lane keeps what is written
rejected: the priests of the four nations

choices.why: tou basileos stands in apposition to Esdra as title, not a second person of the king

choices.term: οἱ ἀπὸ ἀνατολῆς πρὸς δυσμὰς ἀποστρεφόμενοι
choices.english: those from the east turning away toward the west
choices.why: apostrephomenoi means turning away, and apo plus anatoles gives from the east as starting point
rejected: those from the east turn toward the west

choices.term: πρὸς τὸ ἀρκτῷον τῷ ὄρει προσέχοντες
choices.english: holding attention toward the northern part at the mountain
choices.why: arktoion means northern, prosechontes means holding attention, toi orei is dative at the mountain
rejected: directing their attention northward toward the mountain

bible_refs.note: Ἔμειναν ποιοῦντες τὸν νόμον τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ προσκυνοῦντες τὰ εἴδωλα
Ἔμειναν ποιοῦντες τὸν νόμον τοῦ Θεοῦ, καὶ προσκυνοῦντες αὐτῶν τὰ εἴδωλα

pass_b_english: The mountain was called Mount Somoron, and so were the neighboring regions, after Shemir, one of the sons of the Canaanites, before Abraham ever set foot in the land. When the guards arrived, they were called Samaritans, which means guards. They were guards not only of the land but also of the law, for they kept the Pentateuch alone, which they had received through Ezra the king, so that the seed of Abraham might be marked out by this. Yet they did not keep the law fully, and so Scripture says, "They went on keeping the law of God, yet worshiping the idols" (2 Kings 17:32-33).

Since the law commands that idols are not to be worshiped, how can this saying still be fulfilled? The explanation runs in this way. When the priests of the four nations learned that Ezra had settled here, since he abhors idols according to the law of God, they hastened to hide the idols in a recess on Mount Garizim, and they turned the hearts of the Samaritans to pray toward the mountain.

So wherever they are, they pray toward the mountain: those from the east turning away toward the west, those from the west toward the east, and those from the north toward the south, and [those from the south] toward the north, fixing their attention on the mountain as they pray, so that Scripture may be fulfilled which says, "They went on keeping the law of God, yet worshiping their own idols" (2 Kings 17:32-33). For even if they themselves do not know that the idols lie there, divine Scripture cannot lie.
notes: Print is damaged at φύλα89.597 κες for φύλακες; glossed as guards.
μιερεῖς is an uncertain spelling; glossed as written, impure ones, not priests.

problems.quote: Epiphanius says they were guards not only of the land
problems.why: Adds 'Epiphanius says' not in the Greek, turning the author's own direct statement into a third-party quotation.
problems.fix: They were guards not only of the land
problems.ruling: Greek has direct Φύλακες δὲ ἦσαν; no speaker. Added Epiphanius says reframes authorial assertion as quotation.

problems.quote: the impure ones of the four nations
problems.why: Misreads μιερεῖς (a corrupt form of ἱερεῖς, 'priests') as 'impure ones' (μιαροί), losing the fact that they are priests.
problems.fix: the priests of the four nations
problems.ruling: μιερεῖς here is corrupt ἱερεῖς (priests). Impure ones misreads form, loses priests of τεσσάρων ἐθνῶν.

problems.quote: holding attention toward the northern part at the mountain as they pray
problems.why: Misconstrues 'toward the north' (the fourth direction) and 'attending to the mountain' as 'holding attention toward the northern part at the mountain,' making the sense incoherent.
problems.fix: and toward the north, fixing their attention on the mountain as they pray
problems.ruling: Mislinks ἀπὸ βοῤῥᾶς πρὸς μεσημβρίαν with πρὸς τὸ ἀρκτῷον τῷ ὄρει προσέχοντες; four-way prayer toward ὄρος garbled.

edits.old: Epiphanius says they were guards not only of the land
edits.new: They were guards not only of the land

edits.old: the impure ones of the four nations
edits.new: the priests of the four nations

edits.old: and those from the north toward the south, holding attention toward the northern part at the mountain as they pray
edits.new: and those from the north toward the south, and toward the north, fixing their attention on the mountain as they pray

fixed: Removed added 'Epiphanius says': source Φύλακες δὲ ἦσαν is the author's direct statement.
Changed 'impure ones' to 'priests': source οἱ μιερεῖς is corrupt ἱερεῖς, cf. brief's foreign priests hiding idols.
Fixed direction/attention: source πρὸς τὸ ἀρκτῷον = toward the north and τῷ ὄρει προσέχοντες = attending to the mountain, not northern part at the mountain.

problems.quote: and those from the north toward the south, and toward the north, fixing their attention on the mountain as they pray
problems.source_quote: καὶ ἀπὸ βοῤῥᾶς πρὸς τὴν μεσημβρίαν, πρὸς τὸ ἀρκτῷον
problems.why: The dangling "and toward the north" reads as if those from the north face both south and north; supply the implied "those from the south".
problems.fix: and those from the north toward the south, and [those from the south] toward the north, fixing their attention on the mountain as they pray

edits.old: and those from the north toward the south, and toward the north, fixing their attention on the mountain as they pray
edits.new: and those from the north toward the south, and [those from the south] toward the north, fixing their attention on the mountain as they pray

fixed: Inserted [those from the south]: πρὸς τὸ ἀρκτῷον completes the east/west/north direction series and is otherwise dangling.
Left 'They were guards not only of the land': correctly renders Φύλακες δὲ ἦσαν οὐ μόνον τῆς γῆς, no reporting verb in source.
Left 'priests of the four nations': correctly renders οἱ μιερεῖς τῶν τεσσάρων ἐθνῶν per brief's foreign priests, not impure ones.
Left 'fixing their attention on the mountain': correctly renders τῷ ὄρει προσέχοντες; only the missing south subject was added.

last_rejected.quote: which they had received through Ezra the king
last_rejected.source_quote: ἣν ἔλαβον διὰ Ἔσδρα τοῦ βασιλέως
last_rejected.why: τοῦ βασιλέως qualifies Ezra as the king's man, not king himself.
last_rejected.fix: which they had received through Ezra, from the king
last_rejected.ruling: In "διὰ Ἔσδρα τοῦ βασιλέως", "τοῦ βασιλέως" is standard genitive apposition ("Ezra the king"), not "the king's man".
